items.stem: A torch uses a battery, a bulb and a switch. The bulb does not light when the switch is on. A student replaces the bulb with one that works and the torch still does not light. What should he check next?
options: Whether the torch is heavy to hold
Whether the case is painted red
Whether the torch was bought new

explain.why: Weight does not affect the circuit.
Colour does not affect the circuit.
Age by itself is not the problem.

solution: A loose or dirty contact leaves a gap in the circuit.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the circuit shown (P and Q in one path, R in another, S closed) is correct?
options: P still lights if Q is fused or removed
Q still lights if P is removed
R still has its own complete path
R goes out if P is fused

explain.why: P and Q are in the same path.
P and Q are in the same path.
R has its own path.

solution: R's path does not include P or Q.

items.stem: Which statement correctly describes what a closed switch does in a circuit?
options: It stops the current, so the circuit is complete
It lets the current pass, so the circuit is complete
It makes the current, so the bulb lights
It stores the current until it is needed

explain.why: A closed switch lets the current through.
A switch does not make current. The battery does.
A switch does not store current.

solution: A closed switch completes the path.

items.stem: A circuit has a battery, a bulb and a gap. A student fills the gap with a graphite pencil lead and the bulb lights. Which statement is correct?
options: Graphite conducts even though it is not a metal
Graphite is an insulator because it is not a metal
The pencil lead made its own electricity
The bulb would have lit without the lead

explain.why: The bulb lit, so it conducts.
The battery is the energy source.
The gap was open until the lead was added.

solution: The bulb lit, so graphite lets current pass.

items.stem: In the circuit shown, bulbs P and Q are in separate paths. A student unscrews P. What happens to the current from the battery?
options: It becomes larger because one bulb is removed
It becomes smaller because one path is broken

explain.why: One path less means less current from the battery.
Q's path is still complete.
One path has been lost.

solution: Only one path is left, so less current flows from the battery.

items.stem: Which is the best reason for putting a switch on the main wire of a parallel circuit?
options: To make the battery last longer in every case
To turn all the bulbs on and off together

explain.why: A switch does not change brightness.
Its job is to control the circuit.
A switch has nothing to do with this.

solution: The main wire is shared by all paths.

items.stem: Two students test a coin. Ali puts the coin in the gap of a test circuit and the bulb lights. Mei puts a coin covered in thick sticky tape in the gap and the bulb does not light. What can be concluded?
options: The plastic tape is an insulator
The coin works only when taped

explain.why: Ali's coin lit the bulb.
The bulb did not light through the tape.
It lit without tape.

solution: The tape stopped the current.

items.stem: In the circuit shown, bulbs P and Q are in one loop. A student adds a wire across bulb Q (joining both of its ends). What happens?
options: P stays lit and Q goes out
Q stays lit and P goes out

explain.why: The wire gives the current an easier path past Q.
Q is bypassed.
The loop is still complete through the wire.

solution: Current takes the wire instead of Q, so Q goes out and P stays lit.

items.stem: Which circuit part changes electrical energy into light and heat?

explain.why: A switch only opens and closes the circuit.
A battery provides the electrical energy.
A wire carries current.

solution: The bulb gives out light and heat.

items.stem: In which situation will the bulb light up?
options: A wire joins only one end of the battery to the bulb
Two wires join the two ends of the battery together, with no bulb
Two wires join the bulb to both ends of the battery
The bulb is placed next to the battery without wires

explain.why: There is no complete path.
There is no bulb in the path.
There is no path between them.

solution: The bulb needs a complete path from one end of the battery to the other.

items.stem: A student has a battery, a bulb, wires and these materials: iron key, plastic comb, glass marble, copper wire. Which two can be used to complete the circuit?

explain.why: These are insulators.
Glass is an insulator.
Plastic is an insulator.

solution: Metals conduct electricity.

items.stem: In the circuit shown, S is closed but the bulb is not lit. A student replaces the battery with a new one and the bulb lights up. What was the problem?

explain.why: The same bulb lit with the new battery.
The switch is closed and was not changed.
The wires were not changed.

solution: Only the battery was changed, so it was the problem.
